messages.subject: Re: brain registration
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kenta,

Thanks for the message. I have replied below to your registration question (and cced this Google group so others might benefit from the answer).

Sent from my iPhone

> On 13 Mar 2016, at 04:05, Kenta Asahina <kasa...@salk.edu> wrote:
>
> My primitive understanding is that you use nc82 staining to
> "standardize" the brain shape, and project the GAL4 expression pattern
> on top of the standardized brain. It looks your CMTK-based GUI uses Nrrd
> format, which I am not familiar with (I remember I once tried to look
> into this path and got stuck with this format). Is there a
> straightforward way to convert conventional confocal stacks from Zeiss,
> Olympus or Leica microscopes?

You can use Fiji/ImageJ to save as Nrrd.

You need to make sure that you images are all in roughly the same orientation as the template. Ie same slice ordering front to back and rotated around the Z axis to nearest 45 degrees. If your brains are consistently mounted on the slide you should not need to worry about this.

There are also conventions about file naming. These are described in the readme for the CMTK GUI among other places.

We usually use an ImageJ macro when we have a lot of images to convert but you can get started manually. Here is one of the macros we use:

https://github.com/jefferislab/ImageJMacros/blob/master/BatchConvertAnyToNrrd.txt

Best,

Greg.

messages.subject: Amira initial affine transformation
messages.body_plain:
If you have an Amira affine transformation that you want to use, you
need to write it to disk with

library(nat)
m=matrix(c(0.88429, 1.56872e-08, -1.19171e-07, 0, 2.37841e-08, 1.01374,
0.0598496, 0, -1.17784e-07, -0.100796, 1.70732, 0, -72.8736,
31.9657, -7.35532, 1), ncol=4)
cmtk.mat2dof(m, f =
'path/to/myregfolder/Registration/affine/template_sample_ght.list')

Note that the name is important if you want to use this with the munger
CMTK wrapper. In particular the file must end in _ght.list if you want
to use it as an initial affine OR _9dof.list if you want to skip the
image based affine registration altogether (i.e. go straight to warp).
The initial part of the filename must be identical to that produced by
munger in the affine step (i.e. the registration folder ending in
_9dof).

To use an initial affine, you would add the -P switch to the call to
munger.

One possible gotcha:  munger checks the file stamp of the input files
and the output files (registrations, reformatted). It will only run
successive steps of the registration if one of the input files for that
step is newer than the output for that step. Shouldn't be a problem
here, but something to remember.

Best,

Greg.

messages.subject: Re: brain registration
messages.body_plain:
On 14 Mar 2016, at 0:17, Kenta Asahina wrote:

> Thank you for getting back to me quickly. I have a basic question on
> the
> "template brain". Is each group supposed to make its own template
> brain?
> I assume protocol of staining and mounting is a little different from
> lab to lab, which could make the appearance of the brain different.
> The
> registration process shown in your lab webpage uses the parameters
> used
> in your lab, but I wonder whether the parameters could be transferred
> to
> the samples I have been making.

The registration parameters should transfer fine. The staining
conditions can affect the evenness of the staining – this can be
critical for registration.

> Because of the way our confocal works, my stacks are usually taken
> from
> the back to the front. Distance between each image, pixel size etc.
> can
> all be different from your standard imaging parameters.

This can be relevant – especially if there is signal drop off due to
scattering which would result in the back of the brain not being as
bright as the front.

Best,

Greg.

Hi Ben,

On 16 Mar 2016, at 12:10, Ben Sutcliffe wrote:

> I have been giving this a go and the registration appear to run but
> the brain is still not fitted correctly in z.

[snip]

> To generate the initial affine in Amira I opened both brains and then
> used the Transform tools to position the FCWB brain on top of the DLG
> brain, I then stretched it in Z so that it was the same depth. I did
> no click Apply to apply the transformation as this button was greyed
> out.
> I then used “FCWB.nrrd” getTransform in the Console to pull out
> the coordinates (below).

[snip]

> I then ran the registration again adding the -P switch to my regcmd.sh
> file (saving it as regcmd-initaff.sh), but the resulting output brain
> still falls short in z.
>
>
> In the affine folder I now have:
> drwxrwxr-x  1 sutcliff  staff  264 15 Mar 18:17
> DLG_FCWB-01_9dof.list
> drwxrwxr-x  1 sutcliff  staff  264 15 Mar 18:13
> DLG_FCWB-01_ght.list
> drwxr-xr-x  1 sutcliff  staff  264 15 Mar 18:15 DLG_FCWB-01_pa.list

I am sorry, I made a mistake. You should be using the -H switch not the
-P switch.

	-H use Amira's Generalised Hough Transform to initialise affine
registration when available
	   (nb the registration folder should be called
Registration/affine/XXX_ght.list)
	-P find initial affine transform using image principal axes

I think it is ignoring your DLG_FCWB-01_ght.list

Try rerunning with -H instead of -P and deleting the _pa.list file for
good measure.

Best,

Greg.
